newsitem.title: NORWAY: SAS to buy 10 to 15 70-seater planes.
newsitem.headline: SAS to buy 10 to 15 70-seater planes.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System ASA (SAS) said on Wednesday it planned to increase its fleet by 10 to 15 new 70-seater propeller-driven aircraft for delivery in 1999.

SAS spokeswoman Wenche Halsen said the airliner was deciding whether to purchase the Dash 8-400 from Bombardier Regional Aircraft of Canada or the ATR 72-210A from Franco-Italian Aero International Regional.
Each plane is expected to cost around $20 million, she said.
"We have planes with 50 and 100 seats but we need something in between. We have not made a decision as to which type to buy, that will be made after the summer," Halsen said.
She said the aircraft would be used on SAS routes such as Copenhagen to eastern Europe, as well as routes covered by SAS's wholly-owned daughter company SAS Commuter.
SAS Commuter flies domestic flights in northern Norway such as in Finnmark and Troms.
